metric-envelope.physicalInvariant: Generate and regulate a protected metric-compression envelope while preserving curvature, closure, coverage and recovery constraints.
machinery: silicon curvature/control processors with independent references
piezoelectric structural and alignment sensor arrays
metric-envelope.power: Electrical source power, field-former demand, cooling and protected unwind reserve are separately certified.
metric-envelope.navigation: Family-required gravimetry and curvature estimation use independent solid-state sensor/compute chains; piezoelectric channels monitor machinery geometry and structural state.
metric-envelope.control: Regional controllers balance envelope sectors through deterministic links and local interlocks.
metric-envelope.maintenance: Replace and recertify failed functional modules; verify timing, alignment, thermal path, connectors and coverage after refit.
metric-envelope.signature: Metric/gravitational effects remain primary; switching harmonics, buffer charging, heat and resonant diagnostics are supporting Ar'nock machinery evidence.
metric-envelope.failure: Envelope asymmetry or closure instability may be worsened by module dropout, reference drift, piezoelectric fracture, bus partition or cooling loss.
metric-envelope.infrastructure: No Ar'nock-specific metric corridor or beacon network is confirmed.
metric-envelope.scaling: Larger protected volumes require more regional modules, local controllers, sectional cooling and protected unwind authority.
manualProcedure: block transit if a required sector cannot isolate safely

gravitic-plane.physicalInvariant: Couple to usable gravitational/shear terrain while surviving gradients, tides, branch structure and differential loading.
gravitic-plane.power: Sensing, coupling, recoupling, control and recovery are separate loads; speed is not reducible to reactor output.
gravitic-plane.navigation: Independent sensor chains reconstruct gradient, tidal and branch evidence with covariance and source ancestry.
gravitic-plane.control: Regional controllers couple local hull sectors while monitoring differential structural loading.
gravitic-plane.maintenance: Survey baselines, coupling alignment, clocks, transducers, structural interfaces and decoupling paths.
gravitic-plane.signature: Gravitational coupling is primary; structural resonance, timing traffic and power redistribution are supporting evidence.
gravitic-plane.failure: Shear fork or terrain mis-solution can combine with correlated sensor error, timing drift, module misalignment or transducer failure.
gravitic-plane.infrastructure: No Ar'nock gravitational-terrain observatory or surveyed-lane network is confirmed.
gravitic-plane.scaling: Long hulls require regional sensors, load-aware coupling modules and sectional decoupling authority.

slipstream-shear.physicalInvariant: Acquire, adhere to, forecast and safely detach from a Q-boundary shear with valid exit correspondence.
slipstream-shear.power: Acquisition, hold, correction, sensing, compute, cooling and detachment reserve remain distinct burdens.
slipstream-shear.navigation: Forecast Q-weather, boundary curvature, wake state, exit correspondence and adhesion margin using provenance-bearing measurements.
slipstream-shear.control: Regional controllers trim local coupling while supervisory modules protect whole-hull coherence and exit options.
slipstream-shear.maintenance: Check coupling calibration, connector integrity, reference drift, transducer alignment and detachment isolation.
slipstream-shear.signature: Q-boundary/wake effects are primary; electrical switching, thermal load and resonant diagnostics are supporting signatures.
slipstream-shear.failure: Adhesion deficit, boundary pinch or exit loss can combine with module drift, bus damage or insufficient recovery reserve.
slipstream-shear.infrastructure: No Ar'nock Q-weather service or surveyed slipstream corridor is confirmed.
slipstream-shear.scaling: Hull area multiplies coupling sectors and control latency, requiring regional autonomy and sectional recovery.
manualProcedure: detach before uncertainty consumes safety horizon

n-manifold.physicalInvariant: Select a higher-dimensional route while maintaining an admissible, well-conditioned return map.
n-manifold.power: Embedding, axis control, route solution, return conditioning, cooling and re-embedding reserve are separately budgeted.
n-manifold.navigation: Estimate higher-dimensional obstacles, active axes, route geometry, return conditioning and emergence covariance.
n-manifold.control: Regional embedding controllers are separated from independent return authority where possible.
n-manifold.maintenance: Verify axis/parity response, module versions, return references, tomography residuals and recovery assemblies.
n-manifold.signature: Embedding/topological evidence is primary; compute load, switching spectra and reference excitation are supporting evidence.
n-manifold.failure: Axis inversion, hidden obstacle or ill-conditioned return can combine with compute corruption, timing disagreement or reference-module damage.
n-manifold.infrastructure: No Ar'nock manifold survey network is confirmed.
n-manifold.scaling: More span and active dimensions increase control/model complexity and favor hierarchical local control with independent return systems.
manualProcedure: retain coherent tomography residuals as unresolved evidence

inertial-torch.physicalInvariant: Manipulate the vessel's effective inertial response according to the family model while preserving local control, structural admissibility, heat rejection, navigation and safe restoration to ordinary inertial behavior.
machinery: sectional inertial-control field modules tied to surveyed structural nodes
high-rate silicon state-estimation and control modules
piezoelectric acceleration/strain/vibration arrays for structural response
protected restoration, isolation and thermal-control modules
inertial-torch.power: Continuous control power, transient field authority, structural-control demand, cooling and protected restoration reserve are separately budgeted; reduced effective inertia does not imply zero energy or zero reaction-management burden.
inertial-torch.navigation: Track ordinary-space trajectory, gravitational environment, local acceleration, structural response and family-specific inertial-control state with explicit covariance.
inertial-torch.control: Fast regional loops coordinate inertial-control modules; local structural and piezoelectric feedback prevents vessel-average acceleration from hiding destructive regional response.
inertial-torch.maintenance: Calibrate inertial-control modules against independent accelerometry/gravimetry, verify piezoelectric strain arrays, module timing, structural attachments, cooling and restoration reserve.
inertial-torch.signature: Family-specific inertial/gravitational control evidence is primary; high-rate switching, power redistribution, structural resonance and thermal rejection are supporting signatures.
inertial-torch.failure: Control-state divergence, restoration failure or excessive structural acceleration can combine with timing jitter, sensor bias, cracked piezoelectric arrays, module mismatch, cooling loss or power-path collapse.
inertial-torch.infrastructure: No Ar'nock inertial-torch corridor or external support infrastructure is confirmed; treat it as self-contained unless a scenario provides separate authority.
inertial-torch.scaling: Large vessels require regional inertial-control sectors, local structural feedback and sectional restoration authority because finite control propagation and structural modes prevent safe single-point control.
manualProcedure: verify independent inertial and structural references
test regional control modules below transit authority
reserve protected restoration energy and cooling
abort escalation if regional acceleration/strain disagrees with the commanded inertial state

q-lattice.physicalInvariant: Solve discrete Q address and epoch validity with complete protected-state coverage; lattice adjacency is not ordinary distance.
q-lattice.power: Address lock, phase alignment, coverage, translation, exit and recovery remain distinct event-energy burdens.
q-lattice.navigation: Maintain address hypotheses, epoch windows, alias uncertainty and destination exclusion without averaging incompatible candidates into certainty.
q-lattice.control: Independent timing modules preserve clock ancestry and veto desynchronization before commit.
q-lattice.maintenance: Recertify cage coverage, clock phase, resonator response, connector state and carried geometry after refit.
q-lattice.signature: Q-state preparation is primary; resonant sweeps, clock synchronization and thermal load are supporting evidence.
q-lattice.failure: Address alias, epoch miss, coverage hole or clock split can combine with oscillator drift, module mismatch or fractured transducers.
q-lattice.infrastructure: No Ar'nock Q-address beacon or lattice index is confirmed.
q-lattice.scaling: The weakest cage region controls validity; large hulls need sectional cage modules and independent timing authorities.

fold-jump.physicalInvariant: Create temporary adjacency between certified origin and destination volumes and obey the PRECOMMIT point of no return.
fold-jump.power: Nucleation, shaping, hold, closure/ringing control and recovery are separately budgeted.
fold-jump.navigation: Track endpoint covariance, volume occupancy, gravity conditioning, source authentication and topology bifurcation.
fold-jump.control: Solvers may re-solve before commit but cannot invent steering after topology execution begins.
fold-jump.maintenance: Survey topology modules, protected geometry, endpoint references, timing and closure reserve after refit.
fold-jump.signature: Topological transient and closure evidence are primary; charging, synchronization, switching and heat are supporting signatures.
fold-jump.failure: Endpoint conflict or topology bifurcation can combine with coverage dropout, timing drift or closure-reserve isolation.
fold-jump.infrastructure: No Ar'nock fold beacon or prepared endpoint is confirmed.
fold-jump.scaling: Larger protected volumes magnify boundary certification and closure burden; modularity improves serviceability but not endpoint admissibility.
manualProcedure: freeze protected geometry before final solution
abort before commit on unresolved covariance

phase-displacement.physicalInvariant: Map a protected macroscopic state to an admissible nonlocal target while preserving continuity, compatibility and exclusion invariants.
machinery: piezoelectric geometry and strain reference arrays
phase-displacement.power: Preparation, coherence, target compatibility, displacement, rejection and recovery remain separately budgeted.
phase-displacement.navigation: Maintain target compatibility, exclusion evidence, state covariance and independent references through PRECOMMIT.
phase-displacement.control: Regional phase modules synchronize against independent clocks; disagreement blocks commit rather than being averaged away.
phase-displacement.maintenance: Verify module revisions, clock agreement, geometry coverage, transducer calibration, power isolation and recovery stores.
phase-displacement.signature: Phase/displacement evidence is primary; synchronization, resonant sweeps, switching and heat are supporting evidence.
phase-displacement.failure: Coverage loss, target incompatibility or reference corruption can combine with timing drift, module mismatch or transducer fracture.
phase-displacement.infrastructure: No Ar'nock phase-navigation infrastructure is confirmed.
phase-displacement.scaling: Larger protected states require more sectional modules and tighter timing discipline; modularity limits fault propagation without relaxing continuity requirements.

wormhole-gate.physicalInvariant: Maintain a synchronized multiply connected throat with finite aperture, mass flux, remote-mouth state and chronology protection.
machinery: modular aperture-former sectors in surveyed support structures
industrial power, thermal and closure modules
wormhole-gate.power: Hold, shape, synchronization, traffic, thermal and protected closure/recovery loads remain separate.
wormhole-gate.navigation: Remote-mouth authentication and measured synchronization remain distinct from prediction.
wormhole-gate.control: Regional aperture modules regulate geometry/mass flux while chronology veto and independent closure authority remain non-negotiable.
wormhole-gate.maintenance: Inspect anchor geometry, modules, references, cooling, traffic damage, piezoelectric structural diagnostics and closure stores at both mouths.
wormhole-gate.signature: Persistent throat/topological evidence is primary; industrial electrical load, heat and structural resonances are supporting signatures.
wormhole-gate.failure: Throat instability, desynchronization, chronology trip or anchor drift can combine with module dropout, bus partition or thermal saturation.
wormhole-gate.infrastructure: Family is inherently infrastructure-heavy, but Ar'nock ownership of any gate network remains unresolved.
wormhole-gate.scaling: Aperture, mass flux, synchronization, anchoring, cooling and traffic control scale independently.
